summary.text: A P wave, or primary wave, is one of the two main kinds of seismic body wave, made of alternating compressions and rarefactions.
P waves travel faster than other seismic waves, so they are the first signal from an earthquake to reach a seismograph.
Detecting P waves before the slower, destructive waves arrive makes early warning possible, from seconds up to about 60 to 90 seconds for deep, distant, large quakes.

facts.label: Speed–density link
facts.value: Birch's law, found by Francis Birch

items.prompt: An alert system warns people seconds before strong earthquake shaking reaches them. What does it pick up first?

options.label: The slower S waves
The fast, nondestructive P waves
The rolling surface waves
Changes in the air pressure

items.explain: Warning is possible because nondestructive P waves travel faster than the destructive S and Rayleigh waves.

items.prompt: As a P wave passes through a uniform solid, how do the particles of the solid move?

options.label: Back and forth along the wave's direction
Side to side across the wave's direction
In circles like water waves
They stay still while energy passes

items.explain: In a uniform solid a P wave travels longitudinally, so particles vibrate along the direction the wave's energy moves.

items.prompt: A seismometer sits 120° around Earth from an earthquake's focus. Why might it miss the first P waves?

options.label: P waves cannot pass through liquid
P waves fade out after 100°
P waves bend at the outer core, leaving a shadow zone
The inner core reflects every P wave

items.explain: P waves do cross the liquid outer core but are refracted at the mantle-core boundary, leaving a shadow zone from 103° to 142° where the first P waves are not registered.

items.prompt: An earthquake alert system keeps going off whenever heavy trucks rumble past its sensors. What must it get better at?

options.label: Waiting for the surface waves instead
Placing sensors right beside busy roads
Listening only for S waves
Telling P waves apart from local vibration

items.explain: A warning's effectiveness depends on accurately detecting P waves while rejecting ground vibrations from local activity such as trucks.

items.prompt: Deep inside Earth, rock density varies relatively little. What then mostly sets how fast a P wave travels?

options.label: The strength of the original quake
How far the wave has already gone
The rock's resistance to squeezing and shearing
The colour of the minerals

items.explain: P-wave speed depends on the bulk and shear moduli and on density, and since density varies much less than those two moduli, they mostly control the speed.

items.prompt: A seismologist finds that P-wave speed jumps suddenly at a certain depth. What does such a jump usually point to?

options.label: A change in phase or composition
A fault about to slip
A fault in the instrument
An underground lake of water

items.explain: Discontinuities in velocity with depth indicate changes in phase or composition.
